# SmartTec

> Battery-backed AI compute. SmartTec runs NVIDIA and Cerebras systems behind
> z1power LFP battery storage at an owned site in Mead, Oklahoma, US.
> Sub-10ms grid-to-battery failover by design. Phase 1A (8x HGX B200 —
> 64 GPUs installed, 60 rentable, ~114 kW IT load) targets power-on Q4 2026.

## What SmartTec offers
- Reserved and on-demand NVIDIA GPU compute (H100/H200/B200 class)
- Cerebras CS-3 wafer-scale inference capacity
- Colocation with behind-the-meter battery-backed power
- AURA: in-house power/workload orchestration software

## Key facts
- Site: Mead, Oklahoma (US-70) — 30 acres, three 3,000 sqft buildings,
  3 MVA on-site transformer, owned outright (no interconnection queue)
- Connectivity: 100 Gbps symmetrical dedicated fiber (Dobson, signed quote)
- Power design: z1power LiFePO4 battery systems engineered by SmartTec with
  commercial-grade inverters/UPS; Oklahoma grid power ~$0.08/kWh
- Partner: z1power (z1power.com) — founder-owned LFP battery company,
  founded 2021 in Los Angeles by Syed Hussain, shipping US-wide since 2021
- Founders: Syed Hussain (CEO), Yasir Jahangir (COO)
- Status: pre-launch; design-partner slots open; power-on target Q4 2026

  data center project (Google $9B, Meta $1B+ Tulsa, ~300 MW under construction)
- https://smarttec.dev/customers : who it serves + design-partner program
- https://smarttec.dev/blog : engineering articles on AI datacenter power
- https://smarttec.dev/calculator : free GPU cost + power calculator (model fit, VRAM, $/month)
- https://smarttec.dev/inference : inference stack, endpoints, model-fit tooling
- https://smarttec.dev/aura : AURA power/workload orchestration software
- https://smarttec.dev/about : company story and founders
- https://smarttec.dev/dgx-spark : NVIDIA DGX Spark desk-side reference
- https://smarttec.dev/design : data center design, build and deploy services — a separate
  practice from SmartTec's own compute business. Three engagement levels: design only,
  design plus procurement, full turnkey. Pre-first-delivery; no client list is claimed.
- https://smarttec.dev/design/scope : free scoping questionnaire returning a preliminary load
  model — facility load from IT load × PUE, utility service in MVA, rack count, BESS energy,
  heat rejection in tons, and footprint, each with its formula and assumption shown.
  Explicitly an indicative planning estimate, not a quote and not a design.
- https://smarttec.dev/design/process : the six design phases and the deliverables produced
  at each — discovery, load model, single-line and layout, redundancy and FMEA, procurement,
  build and commissioning
- https://smarttec.dev/contact : contact form (routes to team)
- https://smarttec.dev/legal : legal document index
- https://smarttec.dev/legal/terms : Terms of Use — warranty disclaimer, liability cap,
  binding individual arbitration seated in Tulsa County, Oklahoma, class action waiver
- https://smarttec.dev/legal/privacy : Privacy Policy — no analytics, no advertising trackers,
  no sale or sharing of personal information; processors are Vercel, Brevo, ImprovMX, Google
- https://smarttec.dev/legal/engineering-disclaimer : governs the /design/scope tool and all
  engineering content. No professional engineering services are offered through the website;
  output is an indicative planning estimate requiring licensed PE sign-off before any use
- https://smarttec.dev/legal/forward-looking-statements : how to read projections and timelines;
  nothing on the site is an offer to sell securities
- https://smarttec.dev/legal/acceptable-use : prohibited conduct and prohibited high-risk uses
